headline: Phase 18 of BSP_Game_OnMove, 004e50b0-004e525e plus the 004e53b4 fallback. The block runs only when (game+634h == 0 || game+635h != 0), the state is 0Dh and game+7184h is clear; 004cd0f0 is the sole writer of both cinematic flags and sets +635h to +634h AND its allow-simulation argument, so pausing stops the simulation by hiding the HUD with that argument clear. The 4Bh action chain does not open the pause menu: it falls through into the same action-1 test its failures jump to, and its only effect is an early exit to the interface-only branch when 004bfe50 reports no spectator.

reconstruction.cmake: cmake/startup.cmake, one deferred target_sources line into bsp_core
reconstruction.style: one host method per native call site, as in bsp::run_application_frame; the host is queried lazily so the call counts match the native short circuits, including the two reads of game+634h and the three 00425d10 fetches
reconstruction.compatibility: not ABI-compatible, not game-validated; no invented globals, no stubbed calls
reconstruction.test_rationale: the 4Bh chain's fall-through inverts its apparent meaning, so one case in tests/math_tests.cpp pins that the chain suppresses the pause menu and that a plain action-1 press still opens it

tooling_problems: `bsp.py strings <addr>` takes a search string, not an address, and there is no address-to-referenced-strings query; string evidence had to come from `ghidra bytes` on the literal
Ghidra dropped the ECX of 004c40dd (game+30h) and rendered the FLDZ-sourced 0.0f argument of 004db030 as an integer, so both call sites needed the listing

every function in this packet still has an `undefined FUN_xxxx(void)` prototype, so `ghidra proto` gives the body range but not the convention; the RET operands were read with disasm-raw at the body ends
